Looking at this problem, I need to find the number of ways to reach each value $n$ starting from 0, where each scoop moves to the next strictly larger multiple of 30, 70, or 110.

**Setting up the recurrence.** Let $f(n)$ = number of ways to reach exactly $n$. From state $j$, a scoop of type $k \in \{30,70,110\}$ moves to $m_k(j) = \lceil(j+1)/k\rceil \cdot k$ (the smallest multiple of $k$ strictly greater than $j$).

For a target $n$ that is a multiple of $k$, the values $j$ that map to $n$ via type-$k$ scoop are exactly $j \in \{n-k, \ldots, n-1\}$. Therefore:

$$f(n) = \sum_{\substack{k \in \{30,70,110\} \\ k \mid n}} \sum_{j=n-k}^{n-1} f(j), \qquad f(0)=1.$$

**Computing $f$ values.** Nonzero $f$ only occurs at multiples of 30, 70, or 110.

|-----|---------|-------------|--------|
| 0 | — | base case | 1 |
| 30 | 30 | $f(0)$ | 1 |
| 60 | 30 | $f(30)$ | 1 |
| 70 | 70 | $f(0)+f(30)+f(60)=1+1+1$ | 3 |
| 90 | 30 | $f(60)+f(70)=1+3$ | 4 |
| 110 | 110 | $f(0)+f(30)+f(60)+f(70)+f(90)=1+1+1+3+4$ | 10 |
| 120 | 30 | $f(90)+f(110)=4+10$ | 14 |
| 140 | 70 | $f(70)+f(90)+f(110)+f(120)=3+4+10+14$ | 31 |
| 150 | 30 | $f(120)+f(140)=14+31$ | 45 |
| 180 | 30 | $f(150)=45$ | 45 |
| 210 | 30, 70 | $k{=}30$: $f(180)=45$; $\;k{=}70$: $f(140)+f(150)+f(180)=31+45+45=121$ | **166** |

**Verification of completeness.** Between 150 and 210, the only multiple of 30 is 180, the only multiple of 70 is 210, and there is no multiple of 110 (next is 220). So no $f$ value is missed. All values before 210 are at most 45, which is less than 100.

**Checking $f(210) = 166 > 100$:** confirmed. Every earlier value is $\leq 45 < 100$.

The smallest number of jellybeans Elizabeth can collect in more than 100 different ways is $\boxed{210}$.
